figures.caption: FIGURE 5-1 Directional terms indicate distance and direction from the midline.
figures.publisher_description: A man stands with his legs slightly apart, his arms slightly abducted, and his palms facing forward. The directional terms indicating distance with direction from the midline are as follows. Anterior: Front side of the body; posterior: rear side of the body; Superior: toward the head; Inferior: away from the head; medial: toward the midline of the body; lateral: away from the midline of the body; proximal: nearest point of attachment to limb; distal: farthest away from attachment or origin.
figures.depicts: A full-body anatomical figure in the standard position, annotated with arrows for every directional pair: Medial/Lateral across the midline, Superior (nearer the head)/Inferior (away from the head), Anterior (front)/Posterior (rear), and Proximal/Distal along the arm. Patient's right and left are marked. It does NOT show deep vs superficial.

cards.text: The directional term {{c1::distal}} means {{c2::farthest from the point of attachment}}.
cards.why: 'Distal' is labelled on the arm arrow.

cards.text: The directional term {{c1::lateral}} means {{c2::farthest from the midline}}.
The directional term {{c1::proximal}} means {{c2::closest to the point of attachment}}.
cards.why: 'Proximal' is labelled on the arm arrow.

cards.text: The directional term {{c1::superior}} means {{c2::closest to the head}}.
The directional term {{c1::medial}} means {{c2::closest to the midline}}.
The directional term {{c1::anterior (ventral)}} means {{c2::toward the front surface of the body}}.
The directional term {{c1::posterior (dorsal)}} means {{c2::toward the back surface of the body}}.
The directional term {{c1::inferior}} means {{c2::closest to the feet}}.
cards.why: 'Inferior (away from the head)' is labelled outright.

cards.text: The directional term {{c1::deep}} means {{c2::farthest from the surface of the skin}}.
cards.why: the plate has no deep/superficial axis; every other directional pair is drawn, this one is not.
